I have been working this land for 30 years. My mother farmed before me. I know this soil, I know when the rains come, and I know what my neighbors do. My children help a little but my son works in the city now, so I cannot count on him much. I do most of the field work myself, and I hire day labor at wheat harvest and maize harvest. The well gives me water, but pumping costs money, so I do not waste it.

My 10.1 mu all runs on the same rotation — wheat goes in October after maize comes out, maize goes in June after wheat comes out. That is how we have always done it here in Quzhou. I do not change what works.

**Wheat:** I will use the same improved seed I bought last year from the village supply shop — the local recommended variety does well on my land, around 20 jin per mu. I do not buy the most expensive seed. I will apply compound fertilizer as the base when I prepare the bed, then top-dress with urea at jointing in March. I always water four times: once at sowing if the ground is too dry, the winter water in December to protect the roots, again at jointing, and once at heading. I spray herbicide in early spring and spray once more for aphids and powdery mildew closer to heading. I use the rotary tiller after maize harvest to break up the stalks and turn the soil.

**Maize:** After I cut wheat in June, I plant maize quickly — no time to waste because the season is short. I always use hybrid seed, that gives the best yield. I apply fertilizer in one or two goes. Summer gets some rain so I only irrigate when it is really dry — maybe two or three times depending on the year. I spray once for fall armyworm now, it has become a problem the last few years. I usually just rotary till lightly or sometimes no-till if the ground is okay after wheat.

I am not trying to maximize yield at all costs. I want a stable income, manageable work for one person, and not too much spending on inputs that I cannot recover.
